texts.preamble: Vinay Jaiswal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 June, 2018 1 Cr.Rev.No.891/2013 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh, Principal Seat At Jabalpur (Single Bench : Hon'Ble Shri Justice J.P.Gupta) Criminal Revesion No.891/2013 Vinay Jaiswal and others Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh
texts.facts: 2. Facts giving rise to the present case, briefly stated, are that on 28.11.2008 Food Inspector Jeewan Singh Rajak has inspected the shop of Sai Kripa Super Bazar situated at Meenakshi Chowk, Hoshangabad of which the applicant no.2 was the Proprietor. The Food Inspector took samples of Divya Garam Masala, Muneem Ji Ag- mark Great 1 Dhaniya Powder and Ramdev Achar Garam Masala from the applicant no.1 and sent for analysis. As per the Analyst re- port, sample of Ramdev Achar Masala was found to be adulterated. Thereafter, the sanction was obtained and the case was filed on 24.2.2010. On examination of the sample of Ramdev Achar Masala from the Central Food Laboratory also as per section 13(2) of the Act, the same was found again found to be adulterated. Thereafter, vide order dated 4.2.2013 charges have been framed against the appli- cants.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the applicants have assailed the proceed- ings of framing of charge on the Vinay Jaiswal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88727584/ 1 ground that applicants no.1 and 2 had purchased the Achar Masala from the applicant no.3 and the ap- plicant no.3 has purchased the same from Ramdev Products Private Limited, who is accused no.4 before the court below. The applicants have submitted purchasing bills to the Food Inspector and the Achar Masala was purchased under the warrantee as mentioned in the bill. Therefore, as per the provisions of section 19(2) of the Act, the appli- cants, being the vendor, cannot be prosecuted for commission of the offence. Apart from it, it is also contended that sample was taken on 28.11.2008 and the complaint was filed on 24.2.2010. The delay caused in filing of the complaint prejudiced the applicants; hence, they were deprived to send another sample to the Central Food Labo- ratory for analysis. Learned counsel has further contended that at the stage of framing of charge, if there is material to establish the plea taken by the applicants accused, they may be exonerated as has been laid down by this Court in the case of Gulabchand Modi Vs. State of M.P., reported in 2005(1) M.P.H.T. 394 and Puranmal and an- other vs. State of M.P. and others, reported in (2007(1) M.P.L.J. 90). Therefore, the charge and the proceedings be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 4. On the other hand, learned G.A. opposed the aforesaid con- tentions and stated that section 19 of the Act came into operation with regard to defence of the vender during the trial. For ready refer- ence, section 19(2) of the Act is quoted hereinbelow :- 19. Defences which may or may not be allowed in prosecutions under this Act.-- (1) It shall be no defence in a prosecution for an offence pertaining to the sale of any adulterated or misbranded article of food to allege merely that the vendor was ignorant of the nature, substance or quality of the food sold by him or that the purchaser having purchased any article for analysis was not prejudiced by the sale. [(2) A vendor shall not be deemed to have committed an offence pertaining to the sale of any adulterated or misbranded article of food if he proves-- (a) that he purchased the article of food-- (i) in a case where a licence is prescribed for the sale thereof, from a duly licensed manufacturer, distributor or dealer, (ii) in any other case, from any manufacturer, distributor or dealer, with a written warranty in the prescribed form; and (b) that the article of food while in his possession was properly stored and that he sold it in the same state as he purchased it.] (3) Any person by whom a warranty as is referred to 2[in section 14] is alleged to have been given shall be entitled to appear at the hearing and give evidence.
